description: Build the off-model ingestion engine that produces the cached, incremental project knowledge base, and the Python stack adapter. This is the token-efficiency keystone: mechanical analysis runs in plain Python scripts (NO LLM calls), emitting compact Markdown knowledge artifacts the model later summarizes/consumes on demand. Must be language-agnostic in structure with a working Python adapter and stubs for C++/C#/Groovy.
steps: Implement .apia/scripts/ingest.py: given a repo path, walk the tree (respecting .gitignore), detect stack(s) from manifests (requirements.txt/pyproject.toml -> python; CMakeLists.txt/conanfile -> cpp; *.csproj/*.sln -> csharp; build.gradle/*.gradle/*.groovy/Jenkinsfile -> groovy) and file extensions, discover tests, parse dependency manifests, and emit compact artifacts into .apia/knowledge/: project-map.md, architecture.md, dependencies.md, pipelines.md, workflows.md, test-inventory.md, stack.md. Each artifact must be small and factual (lists/tables), NOT prose essays, because the model reads these.

Implement incremental caching: write .apia/knowledge/.index.json recording per-artifact the source file paths and their content hashes. On re-run, only reprocess paths whose hash changed (use git diff when available, else hash comparison). Add a --full flag to force full re-ingest.

CRITICAL: ingest.py must perform ZERO network/LLM calls. It is pure static analysis. Add a module-level docstring and a comment asserting this, and keep the stdlib-only dependency surface minimal (pyyaml allowed).

Implement .apia/adapters/python.yml declaring the Python stack command map: test_command (python -m pytest), test_discovery_glob, characterization_test_template reference, build/lint commands if any, and how to detect 'no tests'. Create stub adapter files .apia/adapters/{cpp,csharp,groovy}.yml with the same schema and TODO markers (commands left as documented placeholders).
Document the adapter schema in a short .apia/adapters/README.md so Phase-2 can fill cpp/csharp/groovy to parity.

Add unit tests under .apia/scripts/tests/ (pytest) that run ingest.py against samples/pyapp and samples/legacy_pyapp and assert: correct stack detection, test-inventory reflects pyapp's tests and legacy_pyapp's absence of tests, dependencies.md lists the manifest deps, and the .index.json cache is written. Add a test asserting a second run with no file changes reprocesses nothing (incremental cache works).
acceptance_criteria: Running `python3 .apia/scripts/ingest.py samples/pyapp` creates .apia/knowledge/ artifacts (project-map.md, architecture.md, dependencies.md, pipelines.md, workflows.md, test-inventory.md, stack.md) and .index.json.
stack.md correctly identifies samples/pyapp as a Python project; test-inventory.md lists its tests; running against samples/legacy_pyapp reports zero tests.
A second ingest run with no changes reprocesses no files (incremental cache proven by test).
ingest.py makes no network or LLM calls (verified by grep for http/openai/anthropic/requests-to-LLM and by test).
.apia/adapters/python.yml is complete; cpp/csharp/groovy.yml exist as documented stubs with the same schema; .apia/adapters/README.md documents the schema.
verification: Run `python3 .apia/scripts/ingest.py samples/pyapp` then confirm the seven knowledge artifacts + .index.json exist and are non-empty.
Run `python3 -m pytest .apia/scripts/tests -q` and confirm all pass.
Run `grep -rniE 'openai|anthropic|api.openai|completions|chat/completions' .apia/scripts` and confirm no LLM endpoints are referenced.
findings: Implemented and verified on branch feat/feat-002-ingest-engine. Built .apia/scripts/ingest.py: a pure-static-analysis off-model ingestion engine (stdlib + optional PyYAML only; NO network/LLM imports). Module docstring + inline comments assert the ZERO network/LLM HARD CONSTRAINT. It walks a repo (respecting DEFAULT_IGNORES + a minimal top-level .gitignore parser), detects stacks via STACK_RULES (python: requirements*.txt/pyproject.toml/setup.py/setup.cfg/Pipfile + .py; cpp: CMakeLists.txt/conanfile/Makefile + .cpp/.hpp/...; csharp: *.csproj/*.sln + .cs; groovy: build.gradle/*.gradle/*.groovy/Jenkinsfile + .groovy/.gradle), discovers Python tests via AST (never executes test code; handles test_*/*_test.py and TestXxx classes), parses dependencies (requirements*.txt line parser + a scoped pyproject.toml [project]dependencies / optional-dependencies extractor since py3.9 has no tomllib), detects pipelines and workflow entrypoints, and emits the seven compact factual Markdown artifacts (project-map.md, architecture.md, dependencies.md, pipelines.md, workflows.md, test-inventory.md, stack.md) as lists/tables (not prose). Incremental cache: .index.json records generated_at, repo, detected stacks, test counts, per-artifact source-path derivation sets, and a per-source short sha256 hash map. On re-run only changed/added/removed paths trigger reprocessing (hash comparison); a cache hit reprocesses nothing. Missing artifacts/index also force regeneration. --full flag forces full re-ingest. Default knowledge dir resolves to .apia/knowledge/; --knowledge-dir overrides (tests use tmp dirs so the committed knowledge base stays clean -- left as just .gitkeep since the artifacts are derived/regenerable and would otherwise describe pyapp rather than the package). Authored .apia/adapters/python.yml (complete: test_command 'python -m pytest', test_discovery_glob, no_tests_detection with collect_command + zero-tests signal, characterization_test_template path, build/lint commands, manifests/extensions/frameworks) and documented stubs cpp.yml/csharp.yml/groovy.yml (identical schema, null + TODO(phase-2) markers). Added .apia/adapters/README.md documenting the full adapter schema and the Phase-2 completion steps. Added 11 pytest tests under .apia/scripts/tests/ (all passing) covering: all seven artifacts emitted & non-empty, python stack detection with no false cpp/csharp/groovy matches, pyapp's 4 test functions listed, legacy_pyapp reporting zero tests, dependency listing, index written with sources+hashes, incremental no-change cache hit, --full forcing re-ingest, change detection after mutating a copied source file, and a static guard asserting ingest.py imports no network/LLM SDK. Verification: `python3 .apia/scripts/ingest.py samples/pyapp` writes the 7 artifacts + .index.json (all non-empty); `python3 -m pytest .apia/scripts/tests -q` -> 11 passed; grep for openai/anthropic/completions in .apia/scripts matches only the ingest docstring's negative assertion and the test's own forbidden-token list (no real endpoint usage). All four adapter YAMLs and config.yml parse as valid YAML. NOTE: `python3 -m pytest samples/ .apia/ -q` (the combined invocation in context.test_command) fails at collection because samples/pyapp relies on its own pyproject [tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath=['.'] which only applies when pyapp is pytest's rootdir; this is a pre-existing property of the FEAT-001 sample layout (my changes do not touch samples/). Run suites per-directory as documented (samples/pyapp, samples/legacy_pyapp, .apia/scripts/tests) -- all green.
